replication.target_description: Relationships of experienced public-service quality and its comparison with prior expectations with citizens' judgments of public services.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title, twelve authors (Chen et al.), DOI 10.1111/padm.12860, Public Administration 100(3), 778–791 (2022) match the neutral replication reference. The CityUHK cover identifies the Final Published version and the text contains the primary report through references. No PDF path was supplied. Graphical paths and their per-path significance stars are absent from the canonical parse; captions appear displaced (path coefficient/metric legend appended to Figure 3 on p. 785). No outside source consulted. Unassigned fields are null placeholders and must not overwrite earlier verified fields. Neutral description does not identify a city, path, or final factorial regression term. It is shared by multiple assigned rows; no mapping from row order or original-page numbers to replication tests is justified. Candidate path-model sample sizes are Hong Kong 992 and Shenzhen 1228; p. 782 explicitly describes final valid responses after cleaning and incomplete-response exclusion; p. 785 gives these model sample sizes and Table 1 p. 787 gives both N values. These are distinct city samples, not groups to sum for one test. Candidate path coefficients include expectation→disconfirmation negative magnitudes 0.968/0.371, performance→disconfirmation 2.507/3.051, disconfirmation→satisfaction 0.274/0.390, direct performance→satisfaction 1.121/1.243, and direct expectation→satisfaction 0.33/0.154 (Hong Kong/Shenzhen). Table 1 also provides different factorial-regression coefficients. Authors give an overall successful replication verdict, with qualifications, but row-specific success cannot be assigned without identifying the target.
